s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly enlarging mass behind the ear with parietal bone invasion and vascular supply
salient_findings: Hyperdense meningeal mass with parietal bone invasion on noncontrast CT
Heterogeneously enhancing lesion on Gadolinium-enhanced MRI
Vascular tumor supplied by the middle meningeal artery
key_facts: History of appendicitis, torsion of an ovarian cyst pedicle, and uterine myoma
No neurological deficits or systemic symptoms
Normal or negative laboratory studies, including complete blood counts, metabolic panel, and viral serology for HIV and Epstein-Barr virus
Noncontrast CT showed a 5-cm hyperdense meningeal mass
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed a heterogeneously enhancing lesion
Cerebral angiography demonstrated a vascular tumor supplied by the middle meningeal artery
Tumor was extradural and caused skull destruction with no intradural involvement

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical diagnosis and histology consistent with meningioma

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular tumor supplied by the middle meningeal artery, consistent with hemangiopericytoma

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Histology showed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm, consistent with solitary fibrous tumor

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive immunostaining for α-smooth muscle actin, vimentin, and desmin, consistent with leiomyosarcoma

shortlist.label: Sarcomatoid meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant spindle cell neoplasm with features of meningioma, consistent with sarcomatoid meningioma

raw.rationale: The tumor's vascular nature, as demonstrated by cerebral angiography showing supply by the middle meningeal artery, and its extradural location with skull destruction, are consistent with hemangiopericytoma, a vascular tumor that can present as a meningeal mass.

rejected.label: Sarcoma
rejected.why: While sarcoma is a consideration for a malignant spindle cell neoplasm, the specific vascular characteristics and meningeal involvement point more towards hemangiopericytoma.
